name: Vision encoder is a separate model requiring separate memory
symptom: The vision encoder is a separate model that requires its own GPU memory, reducing the memory available for the LLM and KV cache. For a ViT-L/16 encoder (304M params, bf16), this is ~608 MB of additional memory.
root_cause: The vision encoder is a separate neural network with its own weights. It must be loaded into GPU memory alongside the LLM, reducing the memory available for the KV cache.
workaround: Use a smaller vision encoder (ViT-B instead of ViT-L) to reduce memory usage. Alternatively, offload the vision encoder to CPU or use a shared encoder for multiple LLM instances.
notes: VISION ENCODER MEMORY OVERHEAD: The vision encoder is a separate model that requires its own GPU memory. For a ViT-L/16 encoder (304M params, bf16), this is ~608 MB. For a SigLIP SO400M encoder (400M params, bf16), this is ~800 MB. This memory is in addition to the LLM weights and KV cache. For a 7B model with 14 GB of weights, the vision encoder adds ~4-6% memory overhead. For a 70B model with 140 GB of weights, the overhead is smaller (~0.4-0.6%). The memory overhead is small but non-zero, and it reduces the memory available for the KV cache. The memory counts are derived from the parameter counts and precision sizes.
